indicators.label: Religion table denominator
indicators.description: People in the KOSIS religion table denominator for the area and census year.
indicators.method: 2005: KOSIS DT_1IN0505 내국인 (명). 2015: KOSIS DT_1PM1502 계, from the 20% sample survey of the register-based census.
indicators.spatial_coverage: South Korea si/gun/gu reporting units harmonised to a 2018 KoStat-derived boundary layer.
indicators.quality_notes: 2005 keeps 미상 (unknown) in the denominator. 2015 rows are sample_survey_20pct.

indicators.label: Religious affiliation %
indicators.description: Share of the table denominator in named religion categories.
indicators.method: 100 * sum(named religion categories) / table total. Named categories include Buddhist, Protestant, Catholic, Won Buddhism, Confucianism, Cheondogyo, Daesoon Jinrihoe or Jeungsan where separately reported, Daejonggyo where separately reported, and other.
indicators.spatial_coverage: South Korea si/gun/gu reporting units harmonised to a 2018 KoStat-derived boundary layer.
indicators.quality_notes: The broad any-religion construct is retained; no denomination crosswalk is attempted.

indicators.label: No religion %
indicators.description: Share of the table denominator in the KOSIS no-religion category.
indicators.spatial_coverage: South Korea si/gun/gu reporting units harmonised to a 2018 KoStat-derived boundary layer.
indicators.quality_notes: No religion is 종교없음 (명) in 2005 and 종교없음-계 in 2015.

visual_layers.label: Religious affiliation %
visual_layers.description: South Korea census religious-affiliation share by harmonised si/gun/gu.
visual_layers.aggregation_rule: reported or explicitly aggregated KOSIS area value
visual_layers.notes: 2015 values are 20% sample-survey estimates from the register-based census.

visual_layers.label: No religion %
visual_layers.description: South Korea census no-religion share by harmonised si/gun/gu.
visual_layers.aggregation_rule: reported or explicitly aggregated KOSIS area value
visual_layers.notes: 2005 keeps the source unknown category in the denominator.
